newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's GDP up 0.7 percent in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Israel's GDP up 0.7 percent in third quarter.

text.p: Israel's gross domestic product (GDP) grew a seasonally adjusted 0.7 per cent in the third quarter, the Central Bureau of Statistics reported on Monday.
It marked the second quarter of slow growth for the economy, after GDP expanded 1.4 percent in the first quarter. Growth slowed to 0.6 percent in the second.

On an annualised basis, the bureau estimated the economy grew at an approximately three percent rate in the third quarter. The Treasury is forecasting that GDP will grow 3.8 percent this year, down from 7.1 percent in 1995 and 6.8 in 1994.

Private consumption grew 1.9 percent in the quarter, or an 8.0 percent annualised rate, which was a faster pace than in the first first half. In each of the previous two quarters, private consumption grew 1.5 percent and in the year-earlier quarter it rose by 0.9 percent.
On a per capita basis, private consumption rose 1.2 percent in the third quarter.
The bureau said the sharp rise in private consumption was due to higher spending on consumer durables, which rose at a 16 annualised rate in the third quarter from the second.
The bureau said fixed capital formation (excluding investments in ships and aircraft) grew 3.7 percent in the quarter, equal to an annualised growth rate of 16.0 percent.
That represented a sharp turnaround from an 0.3 percent decline in the second, although it was slower than than 4.3 percent rise in the first.
In the year-earlier quarter, fixed capital formation rose just 0.2 percent.

The rise in capital spending occurred entirely in equipment and machinery, which showed a 6.4 percent increase in the quarter. That compared with a 1.2 percent decline in the second quarter and a 3.1 percent rise in the first.
Investment in residential construction fell 2.6 percent in the quarter, following a 9.5 percent increase in the first half.

Imports of goods and services rose 3.9 percent in the quarter, after declining in each of the previous two quarters 0.6-0.7 percent. However, exports of goods and services rose 3.5 percent in the quarter, after falling 3.1 percent in the second quarter and rising only 1.0 percent in the first.
